 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/FIRST APPEAL NO. 1042 of 2024 ==========================================================

sentences.text: The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellants - original claimants, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 24.01.2023 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Kheda at Nadiad, in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.326 of 2019, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.13,31,000/- with 7.5% per annum interest to the claimants.

Though served, none appears for the respondent No.2.

sentences.text: Learned advocate Mr. Nishit A. Bhalodi for the appellants has submitted that the tribunal has committed error in awarding the amount of compensation under various heads.
He has submitted that the tribunal has awarded Rs.11,34,000/- towards future loss of income, which ought to be awarded on a higher side considering various aspects.

The tribunal has committed error in taking monthly income to the extent of Rs.6,300/- only, though the income should be considered to the tune of Rs.8,925/- which is required to be multiplied by 12 for annual dependency and by applying multiplier of 15 as the age of deceased was about 36 years at the time of accident.

Therefore, the tribunal has calculated the income and thereafter, comes to the conclusion that Rs.11,34,000/- is required to be awarded towards future loss of income and he has submitted that such amount should be awarded on higher side by considering the above-mentioned calculation.
He has further submitted that under the head of future loss of income, at least more than Rs.16 lakhs is required to be awarded considering the above aspect.
4. Learned advocate Mr. Bhalodi has further submitted that the tribunal has not awarded sufficient amount towards the loss of consortium and only widow was awarded the amount under that head.

He has drawn my attention towards the fact that there are five dependents; three children, widow NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1042/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined and mother and therefore, instead of Rs.44,000/-, Rs.2,20,000/- is required to be awarded as per the judgments in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs Nanu Ram and Ors reported in (2018)
18 SCC 130 as well as New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Somwati and Ors. reported in (2020) 9 SCC 644.

sentences.text: He has further submitted that towards the loss of estate, Rs.16,500/- is awarded by the tribunal which is found proper and Rs.16,500/- came to be awarded towards funeral expenses.

Therefore, he has submitted that the tribunal has awarded Rs.13,31,000/- towards the total amount of compensation with 7.5% interest per annum which ought to be on a higher side and therefore, he prays to allow the present appeal after considering the judgments in the case of Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 as well as Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs Nanu Ram and Ors reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 and other judgments on the aspects in line with the present appeal.

sentences.text: 5. Learned advocate Mr. Rathin P. Raval for the respondent No.3 - Insurance Company has submitted that the tribunal has rightly considered the various aspects and awarded the amount of compensation of Rs.13,31,000/- which is more than sufficient and it would be considered as just compensation.

He has submitted that the tribunal has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1042/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined considered all the relevant aspects, including the income aspect and therefore, there is no scope of enhancement.

However, he has submitted that considering the judgments rendered in the case of United India Insurance Company Limited Vs. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and Others reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780 as well as New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Somwati and Ors. reported in (2020) 9 SCC 644, this Court may pass appropriate order as tribunal has rightly awarded the amount of compensation and no further interference is called for in the present appeal.

sentences.text: It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1042/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.

7.1 It transpires from the record that the tribunal has not properly dealt with the aspect of income of the deceased and the income of the deceased which ought to have been considered by considering the amount of minimum wages as Rs.8,500/- prevalent in the year 2019, as the accident has occurred on 17.02.2019, therefore, Rs.8,500/- is required to be considered as monthly income, 40%
addition towards the future prospects considering the ratio laid down by the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, therefore, it comes to Rs.11,900/-, whereby, towards the personal expenses as per the judgment of Pranay Sethi (supra), 25% is required to be deducted as there are five dependents, therefore, out of Rs.11,900/-,
Rs.2,975/- is required to be deducted and therefore, the amount comes to Rs.8,925/- which is required to be multiplied by 12 months and by 15 multiplier and therefore, the amount comes to Rs.16,06,500/- towards the future loss of income.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the tribunal has committed error in granting only Rs.11,34,000/- under the head of future loss of income, which is insufficient and which ought to have been Rs.16,06,500/- as per the above-mentioned calculation.

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1042/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined 7.2 The amount towards the loss of consortium (widow) was awarded Rs.44,000/- and Rs.1,20,000/- for loss of parental consortium by the tribunal, which ought to have been awarded Rs.2,20,000/- (44000 x 5),
as there are five dependents i.e. children, mother and wife and therefore, as per the ratio laid down by the judgments in the case of Satinder Kaur (supra), Somwati (supra) as well as Magma General (supra), the amount of consortium should be Rs.2,20,000/- in place of Rs.1,64,000/- granted by the tribunal in total.
The amount of Rs.16,500/- granted towards the loss of estate and amount of Rs.16,500/- granted towards funeral expenses is found just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
7.3 Thus, the appellants - claimants are entitled to get the following final amount as compensation:

The amount awarded by the tribunal is Rs.13,31,000/-,
therefore, further enhancement of Rs.5,28,500/- in  awarded amount is required to be undertaken by way of allowing the present appeal.

7.5 In view of the above-mentioned calculation, the present appeal is allowed by enhancing the awarded amount to the tune of Rs.18,59,500/- as the tribunal has awarded Rs.13,31,000/-,
therefore, awarding further enhancement of Rs.5,28,500/- with 7.5% interest per annum from the date of claim petition till the actual realization.

7.6 The respondent No.3 - Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced amount of Rs.5,28,500/- with 7.5% interest per annum from the date of claim petition till the actual realization before the concerned tribunal within a period of four weeks from today.

7.7 On deposition of such amount, the Tribunal shall immediately disburse the entire awarded amount (including the enhanced amount) lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, in favour of the claimants - appellant Nos.1, 4 and 5 to the tune of 20% each of that amount in equal proportion and out of rest 40% amount, 20% each of that amount be invested in the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1042/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined name of claimants - appellant Nos.2 and 3 in any Nationalized Bank till the claimants - appellant Nos.2 and 3 attain the age of majority of 18 years.

It is open for the tribunal to disburse the amount lying in the Fixed Deposit Return with accrued interest to the respective claimants - appellant Nos.2 and 3 on attaining the age of majority i.e. 18 years.
8. With above observations and directions, the present appeal is allowed to the aforesaid extent with no order as to costs.
